item.title: Abandoned barriers, 11th November
item.description:
A drop down kerb was put in at 18 Glen View Road over 2 months ago. The workmen left two large green barrieers that initially were in the road but have been put on the pavement causing an obstruction. We're have some severely partially sighted residents in the street and many elderly residents. They are extremely inconvenienced by these. We have reported these previously but h has been done about them and they're still there. Could you remove these please asap before there is an accident. Thank you. Mike Hurley

item.title: Vegetation overhanging the pavement at 42 Hazelmere Road, 11th November
item.description:
The vegetation at the front of 42 Hazelmere Road is now once again covering over half of the pavement, obstructing pedestrians and obscuring the view of oncoming traffic for neighbours trying to exit their drives. I first spoke to the occupant of number 42 and wrote him a polite letter asking him to cut the vegetation back on 23 May 2019, but to no avail. Since then I have reported the matter to Bromley Council, with photographs, on at least three occasions, again to no avail. Your website states that tenants failing to respond to an enforcement order will see the cutting back done by a contractor and be billed for the cost of the work. Surely we are now long past the time when this should happen?
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Hazelmere Road, Petts Wood, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
